h.reenable.chrome: Click the icon at the left of the address bar, open Site settings, set Notifications to Allow, then reload this page.
h.reenable.firefox: Click the icon at the left of the address bar, find Notifications under Permissions, remove the block, then reload this page.
h.reenable.safari: Open Safari, then Settings, then Websites, then Notifications. Set this site to Allow, then reload this page.
h.reenable.ios: Open Settings, then Notifications, and find the Hub’s Home Screen app. Switch Allow Notifications on.
h.reenable.android: Tap the icon at the left of the address bar, open Permissions, and allow Notifications. Then reload this page.
h.phone.open: The Hub works in your phone’s browser. The bell and the Inbox can show new notices while the Hub is open and in front.

h.timing.more: How soon new notices show up
faq.kinds.a: Hoody writes a notice when something happens to your account. The Get notified page lists everything it writes today. Bots, scripts and schedules do not write notices; their status stays on their own pages. You cannot pick which notices you get yet: every listed notice is sent.
faq.bellInbox.q: How do the bell and the Inbox work?
faq.bellInbox.a: The number on the bell counts your unread notices. The Hub checks for new ones from time to time while it is open and in front. Every notice stays in the Inbox until you mark it read. Read notices move to the Archive.
faq.timing.q: How soon does a new notice show up?
faq.timing.a: New notices may take a while to appear. The Hub checks from time to time while it is open and in front, and a tab in the background pauses those checks until you come back to it.
faq.browser.a: A browser alert is a pop-up from your browser about a new notice. It works only while the Hub is open in a tab, in the browser where you turned it on, and only when you are not looking at that tab. An alert shows a short title and a fixed line to open the Hub, never the notice's message. Alerts are optional, and they stay in this browser: turning them on here does nothing for your other browsers or devices. Your browser may ask for permission when you turn them on. Other Hub activity, such as a Bot waiting for you, can use the same alerts.
faq.email.q: Will I be told when the Hub is closed?
faq.email.a: Hoody does not push anything to a phone or computer when the Hub is closed, and it has no push service. A few notices are also emailed to your verified address: the ones marked "Hub and email" on the Get notified page, such as reminders and stops for paid servers, and news from Hoody. That email is the one way a notice reaches a closed phone.
faq.iphone.q: How do I get alerts on an iPhone or iPad?
faq.iphone.a: A browser tab cannot show alerts on iPhone or iPad. Safari offers them only to a web app on the Home Screen (iOS 16.4 or newer): tap Share, then Add to Home Screen, open the Hub from the new icon, and try Turn on browser alerts there. If the test does not show, that is as far as this phone can go today.
faq.android.q: How do I get alerts on Android?
faq.android.a: In Chrome, open the menu and choose Install app or Add to Home screen. Chrome on Android often will not show alerts from an open page; if so, the Get notified page says so after you send a test alert, and the bell and the Inbox still work.
